proposal.summary: An authorization/sensitive information disclosure in GitHub Enterprise Server allowed a fork to retain read access to an upstream repository after the upstream's visibility was changed to private. The issue affected versions prior to 3.10.0 and was fixed in several 3.9.x/3.8.x/3.7.x/3.6.x releases.
proposal.affected_product: GitHub Enterprise Server prior to 3.10.0 (fixed in 3.9.4, 3.8.9, 3.7.16 and 3.6.18)
proposal.cwe_quote: An authorization/sensitive information disclosure vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed a fork to retain read access to an upstream repository after its visibility was changed to private.

AV.quote: An authorization/sensitive information disclosure vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed a fork to retain read access to an upstream repository after its visibility was changed to private.

C.quote: An authorization/sensitive information disclosure vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed a fork to retain read access to an upstream repository after its visibility was changed to private.

proposal.recommended_next_step: Confirm the fix in the specified versions and backports (3.9.4, 3.8.9, 3.7.16, 3.6.18); notify affected customers to upgrade their GitHub Enterprise Server instances if they run versions prior to 3.10.0 and audit forks that may have retained access.

evidence_quotes.claim: Description of the vulnerability and its effect
evidence_quotes.quote: An authorization/sensitive information disclosure vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed a fork to retain read access to an upstream repository after its visibility was changed to private.
This vulnerability affected all versions of GitHub Enterprise Server prior to 3.10.0 and was fixed in versions 3.9.4, 3.8.9, 3.7.16 and 3.6.18.
This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.
